paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God had already told His people what He wants: act justly, love mercy, walk humbly (Micah 6:8). Then He looks at the city and sees dishonest scales, bags of false weights, and lies coming out of people's mouths (Micah 6:11-12). Our God sees how we do business, and a cheat that looks small to us is not small to Him.

Now watch the "Therefore…" (Micah 6:13). It's the hinge of the whole passage, and it tells us the ruin didn't come out of nowhere. The LORD says, "You will eat but not be satisfied" and "You will sow but not reap" (Micah 6:14-15). I think that's what chasing gain the crooked way looks like: you work and work, and the thing you wanted still slips out of your hands. I've pressed a lot of cookies, friend, and I'll tell you, a cookie stamped with a crooked hand never comes out right.

So what do we do with that? The LORD says it is "sound wisdom to fear Your name" (Micah 6:9), and that means taking Him seriously when He speaks, before the rod ever comes down. The people had followed the practices of Omri and Ahab's house (Micah 6:16), so the question for you and me is whose example we follow. Pick honest scales today, in the little things nobody would ever catch. This isn't the end of Micah's message, so keep your oven warm.
